messages:
Rae: spotting p95/p99 jump in usw1 since 04:12 UTC. big tenant 'data-lab' kicked off multiple concurrent warmup batches. KV-repopulate and NIC tx queues look saturated on ~6 hosts. can we isolate them quickly?

Arjun: Yep saw it. host-level egress spiked, NIC queue depth high, and shared warm slots showing regen storms. Options: carve a tiny reserved slice, apply temporary egress cap + soft-quarantine, or route background work to preemptible pool.

Nora: I prefer egress cap + soft-quarantine first to avoid immediate rebalancing churn. quick command: 
````
rwdctl tenant update data-lab --egress-limit 120mbps --soft-quarantine true --quarantine-ttl 90m
````
This will cap them and let fallback routing handle overflow.

Rae: Good. also enable nic tx shaping on the impacted hosts and flag the job owner to stagger windows.

Arjun: Applying now, patching shaper rules. I'll add an alert to escalate if carveout-required within 30m.

devops-bot: Created incident INF-4401: "data-lab batch burst -> soft quarantine". Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/noisy-burst-mitigation

Nora: Patch applied. monitoring: p99 down ~15%, kv-evict rate down ~40%. a few requests routed to preemptible fallback.

Rae: Nice. keep quarantine for 90m then drain gradually for 20m to avoid cold-start penalties. Also follow up with product on a burst-credit offering for scheduled large jobs.

Arjun: I'll write a short proposal for burst credits + API to request short reserved windows. include cost estimates.

devops-bot: INF-4401 updated: assignees Arjun (RFC), Nora (monitoring), Rae (customer comms).
